key_concepts: Cells reproduce through two types of cell division: mitosis and meiosis.
Mitosis is cell division for growth, development, and tissue repair.
Meiosis is cell division involved in reproductive processes.
The cell cycle includes interphase (G1, S, G2) and the M phase (mitosis and cytokinesis).
Cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm to produce two daughter cells.
Mitosis produces two identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the paren
Mitosis has four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
In prophase chromosomes condense, the spindle forms, and the nuclear envelope breaks down.
In metaphase chromosomes align at the cell's equator and attach to spindle fibers.
In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.
In telophase nuclear membranes reform and the cytoplasm divides.
Onion root tip cells can be used to observe mitotic stages.
